standard_prerequisites: Divisors of meromorphic sections of an invertible sheaf and the compatibility between the two constructions of divisors, via rational functions and via lengths

The trivialising torsor of an invertible sheaf on an integral good algebraic space, its flatness and the identification of the maximal ideals of the henselizations of the local rings of the torsor and of the base
The length criterion for the order of a section of an invertible sheaf along a prime divisor using the total ring of fractions of the henselization, and flat base change of lengths
core_obligations: Reduce the statement to the identification of the pulled back divisor with the divisor of the pulled back section viewed as a rational function through the trivialisation of the pullback of the sheaf
Classify the prime divisors of the torsor: either the restriction to the torsor is dominant over the base, or the divisor is the preimage of a prime divisor of the base
Dispose of the dominant case by noting that the coefficient of such a divisor in either side is zero

For a divisor coming from a prime divisor of the base, compare coefficients at the generic points of the two divisors using the commutative square of henselizations and a trivialisation of the sheaf at the base

Write the section as a quotient of two nonzerodivisors of the base henselization and express both coefficients as differences of lengths; conclude that the two expressions agree because the map of henselizations is flat and the maximal ideal of the base henselization generates the maximal ideal of the henselization of the torsor
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the divisor defined by the pulled back rational function
Split the prime divisors of the torsor into the dominant ones and the preimages of divisors of the base
Compare coefficients over the henselizations of the local rings at the relevant generic points
Conclude by flatness of the ring map and the identification of the maximal ideals
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the compatibility between the divisor of a meromorphic section and the divisor of the corresponding rational function on the trivialising torsor at source lines 2476-2489, label lemma-Gm-torsor-divisor-meromorphic-section, whose proof occupies source lines 2491-2550. The proof is a coefficient comparison that first identifies which divisors can contribute: a prime divisor of the torsor either dominates the base, in which case both coefficients vanish, or is the preimage of a prime divisor of the base. In the remaining case the coefficient is written as a difference of lengths over the henselizations of the local rings at the generic points, and the two sides are matched using flatness of the map of henselizations together with the identification of the maximal ideal obtained from the structure of the torsor. The counted statement records neither the classification of divisors nor the length comparison.
